answers.answer:
In SCOPe 2.08 (current release; periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16) the fragment problem no longer shows up in the classification of these entries. All three structures' syntaxin N-terminal domains sit in the same family, a.47.2.1, so the fragments do not create a separate fold. The 1br0 chain A domain (d1br0a_, sunid 17772) is in a.47.2.1, under the protein node 'Syntaxin 1A N-terminal domain' (sunid 47663), species Rattus norvegicus. The three 1ez3 chains (d1ez3a_, d1ez3b_, d1ez3c_; sunids 17768-17770) are also a.47.2.1. The full-length domain d1dn1b_ (1dn1 chain B, sunid 302344) is a.47.2.1 as well. It sits under the 'automated matches' protein node (sunid 191190) with a Rattus norvegicus species node, not under the manually curated protein node. By contrast, 1dn1 chain A (d1dn1a_) is the partner Sec1/Munc18 protein and is classified separately (e.25.1.1), not as syntaxin. The family, superfamily (a.47.2, t-snare proteins) and fold (a.47, spectrin repeat-like, a three-helix-bundle-like all-alpha fold in class a) are all shared. Parent protein nodes are 47663 for 1br0 and 191190 for 1dn1 B. I did not retrieve 1ez3's parent protein node, so I make no claim about it.

The interpretation is as follows. First, an early structure with a truncated or partial helical bundle is not treated as its own fold. SCOPe assigns the domain by the sequence and structure of the observed region and ties it to the full domain through the family and protein-level grouping. Fold assignment is a statement about the common architecture and topology of the observed helices, not about whether the construct is complete. Second, the fragment structures remain valid evidence for the family and fold but are not proof of the complete domain's geometry. The helix lengths, the helix-packing and the position of the boundaries should be checked against the full-domain structure, here 1dn1 B. 1dn1 B is the better reference for the full syntaxin N-terminal Habc-type domain. Third, fragments can mislead if used as templates or for domain-boundary inference. Missing helix residues change the apparent length, the buried surface and the interface. In 1dn1 the syntaxin interacts with Munc18/nSec1, so the interface in a complex is not recoverable from an isolated fragment. A fold assignment does not imply the same function, binding partners or regulation. It supports only a structural and evolutionary relationship at the family and superfamily level. Fourth, 'automated matches' placement of 1dn1 B means that the 1dn1 B placement is automatic and less manually curated than the placement of 1br0. I treat these domain boundaries and the species grouping as a classification-process detail, not a biological claim that the two proteins differ. In practice, use the fold assignment for broad structural context. For modeling or boundary decisions, choose the most complete representative, prefer 1dn1 B, and compare the fragment entries by superposition and by sequence coverage.

I could not confirm from the API the exact historical reason for the reclassification, so I do not claim one. This answer rests on the current 2.08 placements only.
